methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Robotics & Manufacturing (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 10 same-sector peers exist in Robotics & Manufacturing, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Amca is a robotics and manufacturing company at the IPO stage, founded by Jai Malik and Eli Giovanetti, having raised $76.5M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comp universe of nine peers: one public company (ticker 277810.KQ) and eight private firms including Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, Generalist AI, and Bedrock Robotics.

The peer-median method proved inapplicable to this valuation. While ten same-sector peers exist in Robotics & Manufacturing, the narrow filtering criteria—same stage, adjacent stage, or similar valuation tier—yielded fewer than three datapoints in any category. Applying an all-sector median would introduce substantial noise and misrepresent the company's position relative to truly comparable businesses. This constraint reflects the fragmented nature of private robotics financing and the absence of a cohesive peer cohort at Amca's IPO juncture.

Given these data limitations, a definitive triangulated valuation range cannot be responsibly derived from the current peer set. The analysis identifies a material gap: robust valuation support requires either (1) expansion of the comp set to include later-stage or earlier-stage robotics businesses with disclosed valuations, or (2) application of revenue or earnings multiples if such metrics are available for Amca and peers. Until comparable datapoints reach a sufficient density, investors should treat any single-method valuation estimate as provisional and flag stage and sector-specific execution risk as a key uncertainty.
